synthesis.procedure: One-pot synthesis in which the macrocyclic ligand L forms in situ by [2+2] condensation. 4,6-Dihydrazinopyrimidine (0.1 mmol) was dissolved in ethanol/acetonitrile (5 mL/10 mL). DyBr3·6H2O (0.2 mmol) and 3,3'-(propane-1,3-diylbis(oxy))bis(2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) (0.1 mmol) were added sequentially and the mixture was stirred for 10 min. Triethylamine (0.15 mmol) was then added and stirring continued for 6 h. The mixture was filtered and the yellow filtrate was left undisturbed for slow evaporation for one week, giving yellow crystals of 1. The main text only names the same reagents and slow evaporation, without quantities.
synthesis.time: 10 min, then 6 h stirring, then one week slow evaporation
synthesis.vessel_or_method: one-pot solution reaction followed by filtration and slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered to a yellow clear filtrate and left undisturbed for slow evaporation for one week to give yellow crystals.
synthesis.yield: 21.1 mg (21.5% based on the metal salt)

properties.summary: Complex 1 is an SMM with two closely spaced relaxation processes and a diamagnetic ground state assigned to toroidal arrangement of Dy(III) moments (SMT). χMT falls from 83.36 cm3 K mol−1 at room temperature to 16.36 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K, consistent with antiferromagnetic interactions. Magnetization at 1.9 K shows an inflection near 10 kOe and does not saturate (34.90 μB at 70 kOe). Arrhenius barriers are 18.04 K (fast) and 15.51 K (slow). Ab initio results indicate nearly axial ground Kramers doublets, in-plane circular anisotropy, antiferromagnetic exchange within each Dy3 triangle and ferromagnetic coupling between the triangles; the exchange-doublet span (10.4 cm−1) is close to the experimental barrier.
